correctness.rationale: A nonempty s-set misses a q-cyclic block iff it has a step gap at least q+1. For n≤2q+1 there cannot be two such gaps, giving exactly n·C(n−q−1,s−1) nontransversals and the claimed H(z)=(1+z)^n−1−nz(1+z)^{n−q−1}. Normalized failure b_s=s C(t,s−1)/C(n−1,s−1), t=n−q−1≤q, obeys descending ratios b_{s+1}/b_s, convexity for s≥3 and logconcavity on positive support; therefore p_s=1−b_s satisfies p_s²≥p_{s−1}p_{s+1}, with p0=p1=0 and exact zero-boundary handling. Independently tested every permitted parameter q≤49 using integer binomial cross-products and the polynomial. For n≤2ℓ+1 C_n^ℓ is complete; otherwise closed neighborhoods have q=2ℓ+1 and n≤4ℓ+3 maps exactly into the proved interval. The finite tests supplement, not replace, the rational-inequality proof.
